title: Delhi Court Grants Bail to AAP's Satyendar Jain in Jal Board Corruption Case
excerpt: The former Delhi water minister was ordered to furnish a personal bond of Rs 2 lakh after spending over two weeks in judicial custody on charges of manipulating sewage treatment plant tenders.
body:
• A Delhi court on Thursday granted bail to AAP leader and former minister Satyendar Jain in a corruption case linked to the Delhi Jal Board's sewage treatment plant tenders.
  • Special Judge Digvinay Singh ordered Jain to furnish a personal bond of Rs 2 lakh and provide two sureties of the same amount.
  • The Anti-Corruption Bureau alleges Jain manipulated tender conditions to favour a specific company and raised a plant's capacity without technical assessment, inflating costs by Rs 123 crore.
  • Five co-accused remain in custody; their bail pleas will be heard on September 5.

A Delhi court on Thursday granted bail to Aam Aadmi Party leader and former Delhi minister Satyendar Jain in a corruption case tied to alleged irregularities in the Delhi Jal Board's tendering process for sewage treatment plants.

"Bail plea is allowed," Special Judge (PC Act) Digvinay Singh of the Rouse Avenue Courts said while pronouncing the order. Jain was directed to submit a personal bond of Rs 2 lakh and provide two sureties for the same amount.

The Case Against Jain

The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested Jain on August 18 along with five other accused, including former Delhi Jal Board CEO Udit Prakash Rai, contractual consultant Ankit Srivastava and private individuals linked to the tender investigation.

https://x.com/LiveLawIndia/status/2095434664064475482

The case, registered in May 2024 following a complaint from the Directorate of Vigilance, centres on the tendering process for upgrading and expanding sewage treatment plants (STPs) under the Delhi Jal Board during Jain's tenure as water minister.

The ACB alleges the tender conditions were deliberately designed around specific technological requirements to favour Euroteck Environmental Private Limited. Investigators further allege Jain unilaterally raised the capacity of the Rohini STP from 15 million gallons per day (mgd) to 30 mgd without conducting a technical feasibility study. The agency claims this inflated costs by approximately Rs 123 crore.

"I was removed on May 30. I had no portfolio. Work was awarded six months after my exit."

— Satyendar Jain, in court

The ACB also alleges that commissions from the contracts were routed through intermediaries and deposited into bank accounts linked to several of the accused. A separate Enforcement Directorate investigation identified approximately Rs 17.70 crore in alleged proceeds of crime and Rs 6.73 crore in alleged illegal commissions.

Jain's Defence

Jain has denied the allegations, telling the court he had no role in the tender process after his removal from the ministry. He argued that the work was awarded six months after he lost his portfolio, distancing himself from the contract decisions at the centre of the case.

On August 19, the court had refused to declare Jain's arrest illegal and remanded him to 14 days of judicial custody. Senior Advocate N. Hariharan and advocate Vivek Jain represented Jain in the bail proceedings.

Political Fallout

Jain's arrest in August drew sharp political reactions. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, also from AAP, alleged the arrest was politically motivated ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. "BJP's way of working is to arrest prominent leaders during the elections," Mann said.

Punjab Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan called the arrests "Amit Shah's way of fighting elections," pointing out that Jain had previously spent two years in jail without any charges being proven in court.

The BJP countered that the investigation exposed genuine corruption in the Delhi Jal Board, with leader Virendraa Sachdeva alleging the tender was deliberately framed to benefit a particular company.

What Happens Next

While Jain has secured bail, the five co-accused remain in judicial custody. Their bail pleas are scheduled for September 5. The broader investigation into the Delhi Jal Board tender irregularities continues, with both the ACB and the Enforcement Directorate pursuing parallel probes.
